tldr: The headline layer across all 14 buckets converges on a single visual anchor — protest leaders detained on a landed aircraft and Delhi locked down — with 'detained/arrested/crack down' appearing as the lead verb in roughly two-thirds of titles; the underlying electoral grievance (CEC Gyanesh Kumar's contested voter-roll revision) surfaces explicitly in fewer than a third of headlines, and the Emergency/dictatorship comparison is a distinctly India-domestic and Southeast Asian editorial choice absent from European and wire-service slugs.

silences.note: Off-topic headline ('League, FnV protest Islamic Arbitration Chamber in Padua') — noise cluster hit with no mapping to any frame in this story.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Noise cluster hit: headline covers a Lega/FnV protest against an Islamic Arbitration Chamber in Padua, wholly unrelated to the India CJP story; consistent with italy's near-zero mean_similarity (0.35) in the metrics.

Only non-Indian outlet to lead its headline with a direct first-person quote from Dipke ('We are living under an absolute dictatorship'), foregrounding the democracy-framing before the detention-count or lockdown facts — a sensationalism marker vs. other Southeast Asian outlets (CNA) which led with infrastructure disruption.

Only headline to adopt a meta-political horse-race lens ('As Tide Turns Against Modi'), framing the protest as a Modi approval-shift story rather than a civil-liberties or electoral-integrity one — positioning it within coalition-building analytics absent from all other outlets.

Only headline to foreground civilian bystander disruption ('No trains, no UPI: Rail passengers in Delhi face CJP protest pain') — the only title in the corpus to center non-protester harm; all 40 other headlines focus on detentions, lockdown, or political reaction.

Only outlet to use 'mob' in a protest-related headline ('200-300 students from Punjab have joined CJP mob') — editorializing the movement as disorderly at the headline level while every other outlet, including Breitbart, used neutral or sympathetic identifiers ('protesters', 'student protesters', 'movement').

Only wire headline to frame the movement's suppression as 'unprecedented' in the title itself ('This is unprecedented') — a normative claim rather than a factual descriptor, setting a severity register adopted downstream by several international outlets.

bottom_line: The headline layer collapses India's electoral-integrity dispute into a single image — founding leaders arrested on a landed aircraft, Delhi locked down — with the voter-roll controversy that triggered the protest rendered explicit in fewer than a third of titles, and the Emergency/dictatorship comparison remaining a distinctly India-domestic and Southeast Asian editorial choice invisible in European and wire-service slugs.
